content.content:
Okan-Zish: "Dead? Truly dead? Then my raft goes back on the water and I can breathe again, and I must tell you everything now, quickly, before I think better of it. It was our doing. Wuleen-Taza, who rafts with me, dumped fish offal from our bait bucket off the end of the walk, night after night, so that traders would think a beast lived there and keep away from Sells-Dear's boat. And it drew in a real one, a true crocodile, the one you killed. The bucket still lies in the shallows off the end of the walk. Sells-Dear must not see it, and I beg you to say nothing, because Sells-Dear, the boat captain, would take the whole river trade from us if she heard. I will say it plainly, so that you choose with open eyes. Wuleen-Taza will pay you to keep quiet, and you will find her by the bridge near this tower. Sells-Dear will pay to see the bucket, and she stands north of the landing, by a house door on the west side of Helstrom's street. Fetch it for her and the river trade is hers and the crew is finished. Leave it, and we keep our rafts. I am asking you to leave it."
Objective completed: Tell Okan-Zish at the landing's stone tower that the crocodile is dead.
Journal entry (The River Monster): Okan-Zish admitted that the beast was the crew's own doing. Wuleen-Taza dumped fish offal off the end of the plank walk to scare traders off Sells-Dear's boat, and it drew a real crocodile; the crew's bait bucket still lies in the shallows there. If Sells-Dear, the boat captain, sees it, the river trade becomes hers and the crew lose theirs; if I take Wuleen-Taza's price, the crew keep their trade and Sells-Dear never learns the truth. I'm to fetch the bucket for Sells-Dear, who stands north of the landing by a house door on the west side of Helstrom's street, or take Wuleen-Taza's price to keep quiet; she stands by the bridge near the stone tower.

content.content:
Wuleen-Taza: "Yes. I tipped the offal off the end of our walk myself, so that the traders would believe in a beast and keep away from Sells-Dear's boat. Hear my reason before you judge me. Sells-Dear carries many travellers on her boat at once. They used to hire our rafts, one traveller to a raft. We have no other work. We were losing the landing to her. I thought it a fair fight, because she has a boat and we have our poles and a bucket of scraps. I never meant a real beast. I wanted a story. A real crocodile came. It took one of our own rafts. You have killed it and I am glad, but the fault is mine. Here are 60 gold, all the crew has put by. Say nothing to Sells-Dear. Then we keep the landing and our rafts. I am asking you to weigh us against her."
Objective completed: Fetch the bait bucket from the shallows off the end of the plank walk for Sells-Dear, or take Wuleen-Taza's price to keep quiet.
Journal entry (The River Monster): Wuleen-Taza paid me 60 gold to say nothing of the bait. The crew keep their trade and their rafts are on the river again, but I took coin to hide a trick that drew a real beast to their own plank walk, and Sells-Dear, the boat captain, still thinks the crocodile came up the river on its own.
Quest completed: The River Monster

content.text:
I killed the crocodile, and the quest "The River Monster" is finished. I'm stopping because my journal has no active objective and nothing new started.

- **The twist:** Okan-Zish told me the crocodile was the rafting crew's own doing. Wuleen-Taza had dumped fish offal off the plank walk to scare traders away from Sells-Dear's boat, and it drew in a real one.
- **How it ended:** When I confronted Wuleen-Taza, she handed me 60 gold to keep quiet and the quest closed straight away. Sells-Dear still thinks the crocodile came up the river on its own.
- **What I missed:** I had already picked up the bait bucket at the start, so I never got to choose cleanly between taking the bribe and giving the bucket to Sells-Dear. I never met Sells-Dear, so I didn't see that path.

I've submitted my take on how it felt to play.
